title: rwb-integration composed case-list read and export: ownership duplication, service-base paths, ageing and access-log contracts, parameters, reference data and flag switch not settled
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14, 16, 20, 29, 37, 41, 43, 44 and 45; Ownership Map API (GET /cases, GET /cases/export, GET /queues, GET /admin/parameters) and tables (recovery_case, queue, timer, role, parameter_value, reference_row, feature_flag, idempotency_key); legacy RWB-E2-033 sections 3, 4, 12, 13, 14 and 15; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1, T2, T5.2 and Appendix T-A; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 and Requirements served; Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R5.5 and §R9
section: §3 Preconditions, §4 Flow, §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §12.2 REST consumed, §13 Solution plan, §14 Messages, §15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the unsettled points of the composed case-list read and export. (1) Ownership and duplication: the Ownership Map keeps GET /cases and GET /cases/export with P3 and ADR-020 with DP-19 serves SCR-02 from the owner service through gateway-bff, while the WP splits a P2 APP slice that owns AC1 to AC11 of the legacy key; the composed page and the export therefore exist on the integration base as an additional, read-only composition, and the owner keeps the system-of-record read and its own export. (2) Paths: neither GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list nor /case-list/export is a row of the Ownership Map, and no source names them; they are fixed under the service base of DP-13. (3) Login: no source names the per-service login of rwb-integration under DP-02, and the legacy story runs as the shared recovery_svc identity. (4) JSON names: the sources name the legacy response type of the page and the twelve columns, not the JSON field names or the problem body of the composed answer. (5) Ageing read: the ageing and service-level contract of rwb-case must publish ageDays, stageClockStart, serviceLevelDueAt, serviceLevelState, prescriptionDate and prescriptionClockStatus for a page of case ids, because a per-case read of the timer projection would break the one-hop budget; no source names its path or its shape. (6) Parameters: caselist.export.maxrows is 'assumed 10,000' in the legacy story under DL11 and the page bounds of 1 to 200 are a legacy validation rule, so both become parameter rows of rwb-case read with the version in force. (7) Reference data: LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE and the queue codes in force move to the rwb-case reference-data and queue contracts, and no source names the reference-data read path. (8) Access log: the legacy story writes one access-log entry per export through the RWB-E1-039 interface; the log is a row of rwb-access, and no source names the operation or its shape. (9) Duplication inside the composition: the ageing and service-level rules of BR2 to BR5 are evaluated by the P3 ageing contract for the case-side screen and again by AgeingAndBreachCalculator here for the composed page, on the same owner fields. (10) Edge: SCR-02 is served by the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON and no source fixes that route. (11) Switch: feature flags belong to the platform library by the R-PREC default ruling, while the legacy story reads the flag rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing from the case module's own configuration. (12) Storage: DP-15 is in the pattern list of the legacy key while the read copies nothing, so the per-service Flyway sequence is a build dependency for its conventions only.
evidence: Ownership Map API 'GET /cases' and 'GET /cases/export' owner P3 with basis 'API Specification v4, x-module P3; Arch v5 slide 41 (rwb-case owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers)'; Architecture v5 slide 13 row P2 'Integration' calling P5 by REST and the outside by file only; slide 14 rwb-access IN 'POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits, /masking-policies' with no access-log operation; slide 41 rwb-case owns 'case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers' and rwb-access owns 'Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log'; slide 45 'Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views' with 'REST is one hop'; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 3 'Parameter caselist.export.maxrows = 10,000 (assumed; DL11)' and section 12 'No event is published. The access log entry is written through the RWB-E1-039 interface'; TSD P2 Integration v3 Appendix T-A lists no case-list operation for P2; Ownership Map tables feature_flag 'Feature flags stay with the platform library (PLT, R-PREC default ruling), despite TSD P2 v3 defining feature_flag and feature_flag_change'.
area: Integration (P2) composed case list and export: ownership, contracts, access and edge
proposed: Keep GET /cases and GET /cases/export with rwb-case and serve SCR-02 from the owner through gateway-bff (ADR-020, DP-19), and add the composed read and export on the integration base as an additional, read-only composition on the paths of this story; read the case rows, the queue list, the ageing fields, the parameters and the reference data through the rwb-case contracts and the right, the scope and the access log through the rwb-access contract, one hop each with a 2 s budget; fix the ageing read, the reference-data read and the access-log operation in the P3 and P4 contract stories, with the JSON names in the rwb-integration baseline; keep rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing as the flag name on the platform flag library; record the double composition of the page and the double evaluation of BR2 to BR5 in the Change Register so that the case-side and integration-side answers are tested against each other. Confirm with the DBA that rwb_integration needs no grant outside its own schema.

title: rwb-integration composed case-list contract baseline: page shape, filter names, aging read, access-log operation and path attribution not settled by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14, 16, 41 and 45; Ownership Map API (GET /cases, GET /cases/export, GET /queues, GET /admin/parameters, POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer) and tables (recovery_case, queue, timer, role); legacy RWB-E2-033 sections 4, 7, 12, 14 and 15; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.2, T6.2 and Appendix T-A; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s12 and §R9
section: §11 Data, §12.1 REST provided, §12.2 REST consumed, §12.7 Tables owned, §12.8 Contract fakes, §15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the unsettled points of the contract baseline of the composed read. (1) Paths: the two provided operations are not rows of the Ownership Map, which keeps GET /cases and GET /cases/export with P3, so their exact form is fixed under the service base of DP-13. (2) Page shape: the legacy page returns rows with a paging envelope, and no source fixes the JSON field names of the row, the envelope, the filter set or the problem body. (3) Ageing element: the contract consumes the ageing and service-level read of rwb-case for a page of case ids, batched so that one page is one hop, and no source names that operation, its path or the shape of its answer. (4) Reference data: the read of LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE is consumed through the rwb-case reference-data contract and no source names its path. (5) Access log: the export records one entry through an operation of rwb-access and no source names that operation, its path or its row shape. (6) Attribution: Architecture v5 slide 13 shows P2 calling P5 by REST and the outside by file only, and names no P2 to P3 or P2 to P4 REST call, so every consumed operation of this contract is a call the architecture slide does not draw. (7) Duplication: the contract fixes an additional read-only composition beside the P3 read and export, which the Ownership Map does not carry. (8) Storage: the contract declares no table, no migration and no library row, while the service schema holds the four platform library objects from the baseline. (9) Edge: SCR-02 is served by the gateway-bff composite route and no source fixes that route.
evidence: Ownership Map API has no row for GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list or for its export; Architecture v5 slide 13 row 'P2 Integration' marks REST against P5 and file against 'Outside' only, while slide 45 states 'REST is one hop: gateway to service, or a cached reference read (rwb-access, rwb-source-data)'; slide 14 gives rwb-access IN 'POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits, /masking-policies' and no access-log write; slide 14 gives rwb-case IN 'GET /cases/{id}, /cases?queue=' only; legacy RWB-E2-033 section 12 names 'CasePage of Case' and the twelve columns without JSON field names and lists 'No event is published. The access log entry is written through the RWB-E1-039 interface'; TSD P2 Integration v3 Appendix T-A carries no case-list operation for P2; Ownership Map tables outbox_event, processed_event, outbox_delivery and idempotency_key are PLT library objects created in each service schema.
proposed: Baseline the two read-only operations on /api/recovery/integration/v1 with the twelve columns, the filter set, the breach filter, the order, the paging envelope and the platform problem body; declare the eight consumed operations with the element each read needs and fix their paths in the P3 and P4 contract stories; state in the contract that GET /cases and GET /cases/export stay with rwb-case and that this composition is additional and read-only; declare no table, no event, no workflow and no Schedule. Have the solution architect accept that the architecture connection matrix does not draw the P2 to P3 and P2 to P4 reads, and record the call pairs in the Service Contract Catalog.
